items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Like Eddie Davis and I, we travelled together for about six, seven years. But we had been with Basie for many years. We tried to fashion our quintet after Basie’s 18 pieces.

ctx.x: I would say most of the big bands played for the dancers and I’m a big band fanatic, I love that sound of the big band. There’s no sound that you can duplicate—five pieces is certainly not going to sound like 18. I love to play with a big band. When you’re playing with a small

group, you’re more free to do what you want to do, ‘cause I’ve been travelling by myself for 18­ 20 years, longer than that, just as a soloist. And sometimes I wish that I had enough money to take a big band with me because some of the musicians that I have played with, they just weren’t capable. Maybe I sounded just as bad to them as they did to me, so we had a good (laughs) concert. But some of them as I said before, they didn’t know tunes, and I would just absolutely wish that I had enough money to sponsor a…

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: I went for three months and stayed a year, you know? And that's when Jaws* was with the band.

ctx.x: Let's see, I took a trip to Europe with Basie in 1960, '62. 1962, I went with Basie. I went for three months and stayed a year, you know? And that's when Jaws* was with the band. We did some dates over there with Tony Bennett. Let's see, was that '62? I think it was, because my first trip to Europe was with the George Wein Newport thing. That was Coleman Hawkins, Howard McGhee, Thad Jones, J.J. Johnson, Sonny Stitt, myself, Miles Davis.
